details: Bitcoin has seen a 14% drop over the past week, falling below $62,000. This decline is largely attributed to significant outflows from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and MicroStrategy's first net Bitcoin sale since 2022. Negative broader market sentiment, potentially influenced by oil prices, also played a role. Despite the recent downturn, Standard Chartered suggests that the market bottom may be approaching due to resilient ETF holdings.
title: Bitcoin Slides 14% Amid ETF Outflows and Sentiment Hit

details: The cryptocurrency market experienced substantial liquidations totaling $1.72 billion in the last 24 hours. Long positions bore the brunt of these liquidations, accounting for $1.41 billion. Specifically, Bitcoin long positions saw $626 million liquidated, while Ethereum long positions faced $313 million in liquidations.
title: Crypto Market Sees $1.72 Billion Liquidated in 24 Hours

details: Ether.fi has committed $100 million to a Plume real-world asset (RWA) vault. This initiative aims to provide users with access to yield-generating opportunities within the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem, highlighting the growing trend of tokenizing real-world assets.
title: Ether.fi Allocates $100M to Plume RWA Vault for Yield

details: Despite a general market downturn that saw Bitcoin's price fall below $64,000, Worldcoin (WLD) and Ethena (ENA) experienced significant surges. Worldcoin rose 33% in the past 24 hours, and Ethena climbed 17%. Worldcoin's rally is largely attributed to its positioning as an AI investment proxy by Arthur Hayes' family office, Maelstrom.
title: Worldcoin & Ethena Surge While Bitcoin Drops

details: JPMorgan analysts predict that the crypto market structure bill, known as the Clarity Act, faces a shrinking window for passage this year. The impending U.S. midterm elections and ongoing disagreements, particularly concerning stablecoin yield, are cited as major obstacles to its legislative progress.
title: JPMorgan: Crypto Bill Passage Window Narrowing This Year

details: Ripple is expanding the reach of its regulated RLUSD stablecoin by integrating it with three exchanges in Turkey. This strategic move targets the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, where there's a high demand for crypto-based access to the U.S. dollar, positioning RLUSD as a compliant stablecoin option.
title: Ripple Brings Regulated RLUSD Stablecoin to MENA Market

details: Kalshi has launched the first regulatorily approved Bitcoin perpetual contracts in the United States. These cash-settled contracts are available for 24/7 trading, providing U.S. investors with a new and regulated avenue for Bitcoin exposure and investment.
title: Kalshi Launches First Regulated Bitcoin Perpetual Contracts in US
